task: round 18 RE-CHECK OLD CONCLUSIONS (3 closed/rejected ideas vs new facts)
summary: Round 18 re-check (15:40Z 27 Sep). Three ideas were checked that no earlier round covered. (A) The localisation family (coordhead-v2, full-res residual head, watershed centroid, and float output, which was LB-tested) is the calibration class for exp75 coordinject. Its old verdict STANDS and bounds exp75. A coordinate change made after the CSV is written only affects 7 um matching. The closest measured analogue, float output, showed lab +0.0018..+0.0025 but TIED on the LB twice (probes 32/33), so the true public shift was < 0.001 each time. exp75's lab is +0.002 on 4 in-sample clips, and a0.3 flips sign. So P(display >= 0.955) is at most ~0.3; 'best chance' overstates it. If exp75 ties, run no alpha/MAX_UM ladder. If it shows an UP, it is the one lever that stacks nearly additively onto a division rung (it changes coordinates only, no topology). (B) The secondary-swap family (LB 4/4 negative, plus the probe 5 weight knob) vs exp74 Corwin: the verdict STANDS for exp74. Corwin's own measurement puts the pilkwang secondary ahead (+0.006 public), and probe 5 (weight 0.8->0.5 = -0.002) argues against the suggested 'weight 0.5' rescue. exp74 goes last, only into an idle slot after the exp72 read, and is dropped if exp72 <= 0.953. (C) Speed levers (fp16, fewer TTA views, cudnn.benchmark) and the '~4 h headroom' fact: they STAY CLOSED. Headroom exists only for post-CSV stages (exp75, 10.5 h guard); the 8.0 h per-clip insertion gate still binds everything upstream. Dummy wall time does not predict hidden latency: exp70a took 1,629 s -> (6.87,7.04] h, while exp70k took 1,449 s -> (7.56,7.74] h. So exp70q's 1,874 s is not a runtime alarm. If probe 46's latency is > 8.0 h, its read is confounded, because the gate may have skipped insertion on late clips. Plan issue: the exp73 decision table still lists DC 0.15 rungs (R5/R6), although 43/44 read D0 and 'DC closed on this side'. Remove them. On the user's question: research rounds have run every 1h39-4h05, mean 2h43 (16 gaps since 25 Sep 19:55Z). The last gap (r17 11:10Z -> r18 ~15:15Z) was ~4 h.

findings.what:
Localisation family: v3 FINAL_REPORT (i) coordhead-v2 embryo-robust, full-res residual head, full-res watershed centroid, Ultrack-convention localiser; LB-tested float output (probes 32/33). The 26 Sep ~21:0xZ reading of yuki0731 coord-inject was 'no measured gain, runtime risk'.

OLD VERDICT: refuted / closed. The 7 um matching barely sees sub-um moves. A constant offset cancels. The only channel is near-tie edge flips: one FN->TP = +7.4e-6, so +0.002 needs ~270 net flips. The closest measured analogue, float output, had lab +0.0018 (44b6 +0.0020, 6bba +0.0016) and e48_safe SELECTION +0.00248 [+0.00105, +0.0039], yet the LB tied twice: exp52 = exp51 = 0.950 and exp53 = exp48 = 0.948.

WHAT CHANGED: exp75 = K2 + coordinject (ALPHA 0.5, MAX_UM 3.0) is now on the 28 Sep plan as 'the best chance' (skeptic P(>= 0.955) ~0.35). It is a post-CSV cell (after write_test_submission), so like float output it cannot change topology, linking or divisions (lab division TP change 0). Its lab: kernel path a0.5 +0.00215 pooled on 4 clips that are IN-SAMPLE for the refiner (per clip -0.0029/+0.0125/0/+0.0029), a0.3 -0.00125 (sign flip against the float path's +0.0011), a1.0 -0.00498. Coord-inject's own error medians are 1.59-1.67 um, against V1284's OOF 1.525 um; the alpha-0.5 blend works by averaging two estimates ~0.45 um apart. That is a variance cut of the same kind as float output.

NEW VERDICT: THE OLD VERDICT STANDS and now calibrates exp75. Both float-output probes kept the display, so the true public shift was < 0.001 each time: transfer <= ~0.4-0.5 of a clean 199-video lab gain. exp75's evidence is weaker (4 in-sample clips, alpha-unstable). With the K2 position in the 0.954 bin unknown, P(cross) ~ E[delta]/0.001, so P(display >= 0.955) <= ~0.3 (central 0.2-0.3), P(<= 0.953) ~0.15-0.2. That is similar to the division rungs, not above them. The contrast: V1284 (pre-ILP; it moves linking) gave +0.002 public on exp48 (probe 31). Pre-ILP refinement is the class that moved the LB; post-CSV refinement is the class that did not. Two corollaries: (1) a 0.954 tie for exp75 is the expected outcome and is NOT evidence against the lever. Still, no alpha/MAX_UM follow-up rung (float output tied twice). (2) If exp75 shows an attributable UP (>= 0.955), it is the ONE lever that stacks nearly additively with a division rung, because it touches coordinates only. Its runtime sits in post-CSV headroom (guard 10.5 h). A '29 Sep: best division file + coordinject' build is justified then and only then.

findings.what:
Speed levers: fewer TTA views / fp16 / cudnn.benchmark (v3 (i): 'they change nodes and break the F1-above-x138-by-epsilon logic; cudnn.benchmark only if N >= 175 and nodes/edges match'), plus the task template fact '12 h limit with ~4 h headroom' (R7-RC-C, R17-PI: headroom unusable because of the 8.0 h per-clip insertion gate).

WHAT CHANGED: (1) The epsilon logic is obsolete: finals are #37/#38, and public rungs are class C in aggressive mode. (2) Stacks are getting heavier. exp75 adds a post-CSV coordinject stage (est. 60-100 min on 2 workers, total ~8.1-9.3 h, guard 10.5 h, COORDINJECT_AMP knob already exists), and the exp70q dummy ran 1,874 s vs K2 ~1,512 s (+24%).

NEW VERDICT: STAYS CLOSED, with two refinements. (a) The headroom is real but usable ONLY by stages placed after the CSV (exp75-type). Everything upstream is bound by the per-dataset insertion gate (build_probe_kernel.py l.1423-1434: elapsed since kernel start >= 28800 s -> 'DIVINS SKIPPED (deadline)'). The newest latencies reach 7.74 h (exp70j/k), leaving ~0.26 h before that gate. A post-CSV stack (division rung + coordinject) fits: <= 7.74 h + <= 1.7 h < 10.5 h guard < 12 h. No K2 speed-up is needed, and fp16 / fewer views would be a new node-changing detection mechanism (the 0/5 detection-map class). (b) Dummy wall time does NOT predict hidden latency. K2 1,512 s -> (7.36,7.54] h; exp70a 1,629 s -> (6.87,7.04] h; exp70d 1,320 s -> (7.19,7.36] h; exp70b 1,740 s -> (7.41,7.58] h; exp70j 1,500 s / exp70k 1,449 s -> (7.56,7.74] h. The rank order is essentially unrelated, and latency drifts with submit time. exp70q's +24% dummy is therefore no runtime alarm. But its real latency matters for its read: with L > 8.0 h the ledger cannot certify 'insertion gate did NOT fire', and late clips may have had NO insertion (fewer forks than K2).
